clue.text: Alcoholic drink, cold, can go the wrong way

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the words before it are read from back to front

explanation.surface: A warning that a chilled can of booze may misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can go' looks like a verb phrase about the drink; 'the wrong way' reverses those two words as one string of letters, placed after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a strong spirit and so an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Deceive and attract scorn

parts.note: to con someone is to deceive or swindle them
to tempt is to entice or attract

explanation.surface: A trickster who lures people in earns their disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and scorn are synonyms for a feeling of disdain.

clue.text: Huge lark following carriage

indicators.note: following places the lark piece after the carriage piece

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
a lark or antic is a playful prank

explanation.surface: A giant bit of fun trails behind a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic and huge are synonyms for enormous size.

clue.text: Occupying a pre-eminent position at work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone holding a top job at their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atop is on the summit, placed highest of all.

clue.text: Kind of race problem?

definitions.meaning: an ... race has hurdles and barriers to get over
a hindrance or difficulty standing in the way

explanation.surface: A query whether a race type is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a difficulty in one's way; the race is one run over hurdles and nets.

clue.text: One who may have to make several calls before getting the contract

definitions.text: One who may have to make several calls before getting the contract

parts.words: One who may have to make several calls before getting the contract
parts.note: in the card game ... bid (call) in turn until one side wins the contract, so this is not a salesperson on the phone

explanation.surface: A salesperson phoning round before landing a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Card-game bidding is called 'calling', and the winning bid becomes the contract to be played.

clue.text: Excursion and dance

definitions.meaning: to move lightly and nimbly on the feet

explanation.surface: An outing that includes some dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A day out is a short journey; to step lightly on the toes is an old sense of dancing.

clue.text: Animal food given to horses in China once

parts.note: a cat is an animal
hay is dried grass fed to horses

explanation.surface: Pets and horses being fed in old China.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the medieval European name for China, as in Marco Polo's accounts.

clue.text: A six-footer from near Wigan

indicators.note: from means the letters come out of the run of words near Wigan

explanation.surface: A very tall person from close to Wigan, a town in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect has six legs, so it is jokingly a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Useless — do go on revising

indicators.note: revising the words means changing their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling someone their work is worthless and to keep editing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no-good is worthless, of no use at all.

clue.text: Little rest, sadly, for one having entered the church

parts.note: mini means small or little

indicators.note: sadly signals that the word rest goes badly, its letters shuffled

explanation.surface: A newly ordained cleric who barely gets any sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' is the anagram signal on 'rest', not an emotion; 'for' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is ordained into the church, entering its ministry.

clue.text: Mate snitches, possibly resulting in a beating

indicators.note: possibly implies the letters of mate snitches might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A friend who tells tales may get thumped for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal punishment such as a thrashing is a form of punishment or rebuke.

clue.text: Bird from higher nest

indicators.note: from means the bird's letters are taken out of the words higher nest

explanation.surface: A bird coming down from a nest up high.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sea eagle, a common crossword bird.

clue.text: Skirt's end elevated somewhere above the knee

indicators.note: the end of the word skirt is its final letter

parts.note: elevated means high up

explanation.surface: A short skirt whose hem rides up well above the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of the leg lies between hip and knee, so it is above the knee.

clue.text: Silver wrapped up in note for priests

indicators.note: wrapped up in puts the silver inside the note

parts.note: MI is the third note in sol-fa
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Coins wrapped in paper money handed to clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were Zoroastrian priests, best known as the wise men of the Nativity.

clue.text: City game to lift boycott

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word makes it read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to ban something is to boycott it

explanation.surface: A city deciding to end its embargo on a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns RU upward to UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes what belongs to a city, as opposed to rural.

clue.text: It has wings and flies behind curtains

definitions.text: It has wings and flies behind curtains

parts.words: It has wings and flies behind curtains
parts.note: the wings are the side spaces and the flies the space above, both parts of a theatre's playing area, not a bird or insect

explanation.surface: A bird or insect hiding and flitting behind drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre platforms have side areas called wings and an overhead space called the flies, behind the curtain.

clue.text: His rapport with me may lead to a life of pleasure

indicators.note: may lead to suggests the letters can be turned into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man boasting that getting on with him brings a pleasant life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Hamlet, means a path of easy self-indulgence and pleasure-seeking.

clue.text: One who calls out at court

definitions.text: One who calls out at court

parts.words: One who calls out at court
parts.note: the court is a tennis court, and calling out means ruling a ball outside the lines, not a court usher

explanation.surface: A court official announcing names in a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this official watches a line and calls a ball out when it lands beyond it.

clue.text: Cooking tripe, say, may lead to acrimony

indicators.note: cooking the words means mixing them up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Serving up tripe may start an argument at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness of tone or manner, close in meaning to bitterness.

clue.text: London profits from this form of taxation?

definitions.text: London profits from this form of taxation?

parts.words: London profits from this form of taxation?
parts.note: London is the capital, and when it profits it gains, so the tax name can be read as a city getting richer

explanation.surface: Asking whether the capital benefits from a particular tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax is levied on profit from selling assets; read literally it is the capital city gaining.

clue.text: Popular move, building arch

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a step is a move, as in dance

explanation.surface: A well-liked development in the building of an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle part of the foot.

clue.text: No parking for waiting in terminal

indicators.note: no parking says the parking letter must go

parts.note: pending means waiting to be decided
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: No parking spaces available for those waiting at a terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the last part or close of something, the same as its finish.

clue.text: They often have to kneel in an unsophisticated life

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: People leading a simple life who must often kneel.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of religious orders of women kneel often in prayer.

clue.text: Shelter behind this person in affray

indicators.note: behind puts the shelter piece after the setter piece

parts.note: this person is the setter, so ME
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone hiding behind the speaker during a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused fight or scuffle, as is an affray.

clue.text: I object to Scripture lessons being simple

parts.note: ME is the object form of the pronoun I
RE is religious education, the school subject once called Scripture in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that Bible classes are too easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' looks like a protest; it means I in the objective case.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child', i.e. simple or bare.

clue.text: Bird seen when others rise

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, so other birds

explanation.surface: A bird spotted as the rest of the flock takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means other birds, the auks; 'rise' turns them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a predatory seabird that robs gulls of food.

clue.text: Further chaos in Laos

indicators.note: chaos in the word Laos means its letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: More disorder in the South-East Asian country Laos.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and further both mean in addition, besides.

clue.text: Burly but brainless group

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid or brainless
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Muscular but dim people in a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset and burly both describe a stocky, heavily built body.

clue.text: Students of the past

parts.note: not historians studying history but people who were once pupils at a school or college

explanation.definitionFit: Graduates or former pupils of a school or university are its old students.

clue.text: Long time in short trousers and spectacles

indicators.note: in puts the long time inside the trousers

parts.note: pants are short for pantaloons, i.e. trousers (US sense)
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Wearing shorts for years, with glasses on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests glasses; it means grand public shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageants are elaborate public shows or processions, i.e. spectacles.

clue.text: Its captain was really put off by the crew

definitions.text: Its captain was really put off by the crew

parts.words: Its captain was really put off by the crew
parts.note: the mutineers literally put Captain Bligh off the ship in a small boat in 1789, not just irritated him

explanation.surface: A skipper whose sailors thoroughly disheartened him.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Bounty's crew mutinied and set Captain William Bligh adrift in the ship's launch.
